q: In rotational motion, the angular momentum of an object is defined as the product of its ____ and the angular velocity.
e: Angular momentum ($L$) is the rotational analog of linear momentum, calculated as $L = I\omega$.

q: For linear motion, the momentum is equal to the product of the ____ and the velocity.
e: Linear momentum ($p$) is defined as $p = mv$, where mass is the measure of inertia in linear motion.

q: The moment of inertia is analogous to mass and the angular velocity is analogous to the ____.
e: Rotational kinematic quantities have direct analogs in linear kinematics.

q: The formula for angular momentum is ____.
e: This equation defines angular momentum as the product of rotational inertia and rotational speed.

q: In SI units, since the unit of moment of inertia is $kg \cdot m^2$ and that of angular velocity is $rad \cdot s^{-1}$, the unit of angular momentum is ____.
e: Multiplying the units of moment of inertia and angular velocity yields the SI unit for angular momentum.
Angular momentum has both magnitude and a specific direction determined by the right-hand rule.

q: The law of ____ is also one fundamental law of physics.
e: This law states that angular momentum remains constant in the absence of external torques.

q: This law states that: If there is no ____ acting on an isolated system, the total angular momentum of the system is constant.
e: Just as linear momentum is conserved when net external force is zero, angular momentum is conserved when net external torque is zero.
This is the mathematical representation of the conservation of angular momentum.

q: Her rate of spin (angular speed) increases greatly as her ____ decreases by pulling in her arms inwards.
e: By pulling her arms in, the skater reduces her moment of inertia, causing her angular velocity to increase to conserve angular momentum.

q: If she wants to slow down her rotation, she will stretch her arms ____.
e: Stretching arms outwards increases the moment of inertia, which correspondingly decreases the angular speed.

q: When her moment of inertia increases, the rotational angular speed will ____.
e: Angular speed and moment of inertia are inversely proportional when angular momentum is conserved.

q: An example of conservation of angular momentum is seen in an ____ performing a spin.
e: Ice skaters demonstrate this principle visibly by changing their body configuration to alter their spin rate.

q: A ____ who is rotating when jumping off the board does not need to make any physical effort to continue rotating.
e: Once in the air, the diver is an isolated system with negligible external torque, so their angular momentum is conserved.

q: The moment of inertia of a disc is given by the formula ____.
e: This is the standard moment of inertia for a uniform solid disc or cylinder rotating about its central axis.
